correctness.rationale: Invertibility of the target square list makes the images of distinct natural basis vectors have disjoint supports. Thus the matrix is monomial and its permutation is a rotation. For the diagonal basis-change recursion the last exponent ranges over a coset of the image of multiplication by 2^n−1 modulo Q, so the weighted sum modulo g is complete; rotations multiply it by powers of 2. At additive order d the orbit length is h, and the lifts of a rotation by k solve (2^n−1)u₀=a(1−2^k) modulo Q, with exactly g lifts if h divides k and zero otherwise. For h<n, taking the (n/h)-th power of a lift of rotation by h gives first exponent Su₀+a, S=(2^n−1)/(2^h−1). Vanishing suffices for the whole diagonal map and implies the lift congruence. Since gcd(Q,S) divides g, solvability is equivalent to gcd(Q,S) dividing gcd(g,a)=g/d. The trivial quotient h=n and g=1 cases agree. The cycle also makes any ideal containing a nonzero vector contain a basis vector by multiplying at a nonzero coordinate, then all basis vectors by squaring. In the disputed six-cycle over F₇ with last weight 3, writing 3 as generator, a lift of shift 2 must have odd first exponent u. Its cube then has first exponent 21u+1=4 mod 6, so no lift of that generator has order three. For example the exponents (1,2,4,2,5,4) give an explicit lift whose cube scales e₀ by 4. This check uses the actual rotation image, not extension-field points.
residual_risks: Finite congruence sweeps in the frozen verification are illustrative; the result rests on the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the arbitrary-field-size, all-n arithmetic classification with a classwise splitting test for the actual finite-field rotation image. Prior monomial and group-scheme structures and low-dimensional cases are credited. The same-day F₄ classification gives exact narrower overlap, without a same-day priority inference. A next-day arbitrary-q record duplicates the orbit and order formulas but does not give the splitting test. The apparent broader splitting assertion in arXiv:2505.14584 does not imply the test: if graph arrows include the scale tuple, the weighted graph automorphism group already includes diagonal maps; if one forgets the tuple to obtain the actual permutation image in Notation 6.16, choosing a lift is not a homomorphism. The explicit nonsplit F₇ example distinguishes the interpretations.
residual_risks: Ranked catalogue inspection is not exhaustive worldwide priority. Same-day relative priority in the F₄ case was not established.
The objection to the 2LI splitting assertion is limited to the sequence onto the actual permutation image; it is not a judgment about unrelated results in that paper.

value.rationale: A uniform classification of all finite-field forms of an oriented cycle makes the dependence on both the field and weights explicit. The arithmetic section test gives information beyond both the order and graph symmetry; order-three rotation images in the F₇ and F₁₉ six-cycle examples exhibit different extension behavior. The criterion answers a natural concrete instance of a general splitting question without claiming to settle that question for all perfect evolution algebras.
residual_risks: Only a single oriented cycle and rational linear automorphisms are classified.
